run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: The requested Datadog APM data does not exist in this Run: the available data sources are Elasticsearch, Jaeger, Kubernetes and Prometheus (only change_history is listed as not integrated), and every Jaeger (traces_search, traces_search_by_tags, traces_query_trace_by_id, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations) and Prometheus (get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_series, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules) call returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on target m0-otel-20260909, and elasticsearch_list_indices matched no index. Consequently no span, span-duration, RPC-client or request-latency series for `checkout` (or `checkout-service`) could be read, and I cannot name which downstream call was slow. What the reachable evidence does show: all 21 otel-demo deployments (checkout, payment, shipping, currency, cart, product-catalog, email, quote, frontend, …) report 1/1 ready replicas and all 22 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready; the checkout container's own logs for 05:46:55–06:27:18 show only severity "info" lines with complete order sequences, each "payment went through" line following the "[PlaceOrder]" line by ~11–20 ms and the confirmation-email line following payment by ~8–14 ms (sample orders at 06:26:18.563578557 → 06:26:18.578522097 → 06:26:18.587849477); no error/warning lines were returned for checkout, payment, shipping, cart or product-catalog in the queried windows; the demo's fault-injection flags in the flagd-config ConfigMap are all state ENABLED but every defaultVariant is "off"; the only Kubernetes event inside the window is an unrelated Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for service app-282/loki at 05:28:04. Two observed instrumentation facts remain unexplained as latency causes: the otel-collector logs a metric-upload failure every 10 s from at least 05:43:22 to 06:27:52 ("http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large … frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header"), and Prometheus itself is ingesting OTLP writes while the read path used by this Run was unavailable. These are recorded as hypotheses and gaps, not as a root cause; root_cause is null.

claims.text: All 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo, including checkout, payment, shipping, currency, cart, product-catalog, email, quote and frontend, reported spec.replicas=1 with status.readyReplicas=1 and status.availableReplicas=1 at the time of the query; image tags are ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-<service>.

The 22 pods of namespace otel-demo (ad, alertmanager-0, cart, checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) were all in phase Running with ready containers; restart counts were 1 for the application pods, 2 for kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz and 3 for prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn, with pod start times 2026-11-20T16:32–16:33.

In the 200 newest lines of pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (container checkout, current instance, 05:46:55.432–06:27:18.807, 94 older lines omitted by the limit), every log entry is severity "info" and consists of repeating triples "[PlaceOrder] user_id=…" → "payment went through (transaction_id: …)" → "order confirmation email sent to …"; for example 06:26:18.563578557 ([PlaceOrder]) → 06:26:18.578522097 (payment, ~15 ms later) → 06:26:18.587849477 (email, ~9 ms after payment), and 06:24:36.491505625 → 06:24:36.508817569 → 06:24:36.517030974.

The flagd-config ConfigMap key demo.flagd.json lists the fault/latency flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with state "ENABLED" but defaultVariant "off" (kafkaQueueProblems and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage off=0, imageSlowLoad off=0 with 5sec/10sec variants, paymentFailure off=0).

The only Kubernetes event whose timestamp lies inside 2026-11-20T06:27:55–2026-11-21T06:27:55 is a Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint at 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z for involvedObject.kind Endpoints, name lukt-related service app-282/loki, message "Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints \"loki\" already exists"; no event in the window concerns an otel-demo pod or the checkout service.

Pod otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c (container opentelemetry-collector) logs the exact error "failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header\"" at 10-second intervals from at least 2026-11-21T05:43:22Z through 2026-11-21T06:27:52Z (102 matching lines in 05:27:55–05:45:00, 391 in 05:27:55–06:27:55), together with grpc client warnings "addrConn.createTransport failed to connect to {Addr: \"10.96.247.55:4318\", ServerName: \"otel-collector:4318\"}".

The otel-collector ConfigMap key "relay" configures the metrics pipeline exporter otlphttp/prometheus with endpoint http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp (basicauth user collector), the traces pipeline exporter otlp with endpoint jaeger-collector:4317, the logs pipeline exporter opensearch with endpoint http://opensearch:9200, and internal telemetry metrics via a periodic reader whose otlp exporter targets otel-collector:4318 with protocol grpc.

In 06:20:00–06:27:55 the otel-collector debug exporter continuously reports received trace batches up to 2026-11-21T06:27:54.821Z (e.g. "Traces … resource spans: 1, spans: 13" at 06:27:49.865Z and "resource spans: 1, spans: 2" at 06:27:54.079Z), so spans were still being received and exported during the reported slow-checkout hour.

Pod prometheus-9bc78b5f7-c9wx8 (container prometheus-server) logs recurring WARN "Error on ingesting out-of-order exemplars" (component=web, num_dropped=6–10) roughly once per minute from 2026-11-21T06:18:48.929Z to 06:27:49.127Z, which shows Prometheus was accepting OTLP metric writes during the incident hour.

Services and endpoints exist for the telemetry backends in otel-demo: prometheus ClusterIP 10.96.120.134:9090 (endpoint 10.244.0.5), prometheus-readonly-proxy NodePort 10.96.17.18:9090 (endpoint 10.244.0.2), jaeger-collector with ports 9411/14250/14267/14268/4317/4318 and jaeger-query 16686/16685 (both endpoint 10.244.0.11); the jaeger container last terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 reason Unknown (restartCount 1) and the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx container last terminated at 2026-11-21T04:24:10Z with exitCode 1 reason Error (restartCount 3), both currently Running and Ready — i.e. their restarts precede the 05:27:55–06:27:55 incident hour.

If a checkout dependency was slow during the hour, the candidates are the calls checkout makes in its PlaceOrder path — cart (GetCart/EmptyCart), product-catalog (GetProduct), currency (ConvertCurrency), shipping (GetQuote/ShipOrder), payment (Charge) and email (SendOrderConfirmation). The checkout log timings only narrow this to the pre-payment segment (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping quote) because payment and email can be seen completing ~15 ms and ~24 ms after the [PlaceOrder] line in sampled orders; span durations or RPC-client percentiles would be needed to name the slow call.

The inability of this Run to read Jaeger traces and Prometheus series may be a read-path problem rather than an empty pipeline: trace batches were still being received by otel-collector and exported to jaeger-collector:4317 up to 06:27:54, Prometheus was ingesting OTLP writes through 06:27:49, and both backend services have endpoints, while every traces_* and Prometheus tool call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

The otel-collector's own telemetry reader is misconfigured as gRPC against its HTTP OTLP port (otlp exporter, protocol grpc, endpoint otel-collector:4318, while the receiver serves OTLP/HTTP on 4318 and gRPC on 4317), which matches the repeated "http2: frame too large … looked like an HTTP/1.1 header" upload failures; this would degrade collector self-telemetry, but no evidence ties it to request latency in checkout.

Fault injection via flagd is not supported by the configuration read at query time: all eleven fault/latency flags in flagd-config have defaultVariant "off", including cartFailure, paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and the latency flags imageSlowLoad (off=0) and kafkaQueueProblems (off=0).

There is no evidence of checkout-side failure in the sampled logs: the 200 newest checkout container lines contain only severity "info" order-flow messages, and the checkout container logged no line matching error|fail|timeout|deadline|refus|panic|warn in the 05:27:55–05:50:00 sub-window that was queried.

Rejected: that a pod-level failure (crash, eviction, OOM, readiness failure) of checkout or one of its dependencies explains the reported slowness. All 22 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, the application containers show restart counts of 1 matching their 2026-11-20 start, and the only event inside the window is a Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for service app-282/loki at 05:28:04, which concerns Endpoints, not a demo workload.

To answer the original question, obtain a working APM read path: either grant Datadog APM access (it is not among the available data sources here) or repair the Jaeger/Prometheus read access used by the investigation tooling, then compare per-operation latency for checkout's client spans to cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, payment and email (e.g. rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name="checkout"} by rpc_service/rpc_method and p95) against a pre-incident baseline window.

Have a human correct the otel-collector internal telemetry exporter so it does not send gRPC to otel-collector:4318 (the OTLP/HTTP port) — e.g. use protocol http/protobuf against 4318 or gRPC against 4317 — to stop the 10-second "frame too large / HTTP/1.1 header" upload failures and restore collector self-telemetry.

gaps: Datadog APM is not an available data source in this Run (available: elasticsearch, jaeger, kubernetes, prometheus; not integrated: change_history), so no Datadog trace, span or APM latency data could be examined at all.

Every Jaeger tool call failed: traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search (service checkout and service frontend), traces_search_by_tags and traces_query_trace_by_id each returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on target m0-otel-20260909, so no span durations, no parent-child call edges and no per-operation slow-call ranking could be read. Because no service/operation list could be retrieved, the exact service name could not be verified either: the tool's declared available-service list contains "checkout", not the requested "checkout-service", but neither name could be queried successfully.

Every Prometheus tool call failed with status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on target m0-otel-20260909 (get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_series, get_metric_metadata not used, metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count/bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and the kube-state-metrics series could not be read; missing series values are unknown, not zero.

elasticsearch_list_indices with pattern "*" returned status no_data with zero indices, so no log-search confirmation of checkout latency or error text is possible; this is an empty result of that query, not proof that nothing was logged.

No log line in the reachable containers records a request or downstream-call duration, so total checkout latency and per-dependency latency are not measurable from logs; the checkout timing gaps quoted (PlaceOrder→payment ~11–20 ms, payment→email ~8–14 ms) only cover the log-emitted steps of sampled orders and cannot establish end-to-end latency.

Whether any downstream call actually became slower during 2026-11-21T05:27:55–06:27:55 — and which one — is unknown; the reported customer-visible slowness could not be corroborated or timed, and no pre-incident latency baseline exists in the evidence, so no latency trend is claimed.

The cause of the SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE read failures for the Prometheus/Jaeger tools is unknown: Prometheus was ingesting OTLP writes and otel-collector was still exporting spans to jaeger-collector:4317 during the window, and both backend services have endpoints, but the gateway-side read failure could not be diagnosed from cluster objects or pod logs.

Whether the otel-collector's 10-second metric upload failures affected application telemetry (as opposed to the collector's own internal telemetry reader pointed at otel-collector:4318) could not be determined, because no metric ingestion state was readable.

Earlier parts of the hour were only partially sampled: checkout logs showed the newest 200 of 294 lines (oldest 94 omitted), the otel-collector error listing showed the newest 60 of 391 and newest 10 of 102 matching lines, and payment/shipping/cart/product-catalog error-filtered log queries returned no matching lines (an empty result, not proof of absence).
next_steps: Restore or provide read access to the APM backend (Datadog, or the Jaeger query and Prometheus read paths used by the tooling) for the window 2026-11-21T05:27:55Z–06:27:55Z, then rank checkout client spans by duration per downstream service/method and compare with a pre-05:27 baseline.

If Prometheus access is restored, check rpc_client_duration_milliseconds for service_name="checkout" broken out by rpc_service and rpc_method, plus traces_span_metrics_calls_total by span_name and status_code, to isolate which of cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, payment or email deviates.

Have a human review the otel-collector internal telemetry exporter configuration (gRPC to otel-collector:4318) and the prometheus-readonly-proxy nginx read path, which restarted 3 times at ~04:24Z, before the incident window.

Confirm whether the customer reports concern the same cluster (production-eu-west-2 / namespace otel-demo) and the same hour, since no trace or metric evidence for the reported slowness could be obtained.

content.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
